ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
As shown in the figure, the wooden rod is $5\mathrm{m}$ long, with its upper end fixed at a certain point. It is released from rest and allowed to fall freely (ignoring air resistance). The wooden rod passes through the cylinder $AB$, which is located $20\mathrm{m}$ directly below the suspension point. The height of cylinder $AB$ is $5\mathrm{m}$, and $g$ is taken as $10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$.

1. The time $t_{1}$ it takes for the wooden rod to pass through the upper end $A$ of the cylinder.
2. The time $t_{2}$ it takes for the wooden rod to pass through the cylinder

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, a wooden rod is vertically suspended below an upper support point, and below it there is a vertical cylinder. The upper end of the cylinder is labeled A, and near the lower end it is labeled B; the vertical arrow in the figure marks the distance from the upper suspension point to the horizontal plane where the upper end A of the cylinder is located as 20 m. The problem also gives that the wooden rod is 5 m long, and the cylinder AB is 5 m high. Reasoning: After release, the wooden rod undergoes free fall. All points on the rigid body fall the same distance at the same moment, and starting from rest satisfies s = (1/2)gt^2 = 5t^2. The initial position of the lower end of the wooden rod is 5 m lower than the suspension point, so when the lower end reaches A, the wooden rod as a whole only needs to fall 20 - 5 = 15 m, so the absolute time of entering A is T_enter = sqrt(15/5) = sqrt(3) s. When the upper end of the wooden rod reaches A, it needs to fall 20 m from the suspension point, so T_topA = sqrt(20/5) = 2 s. Therefore the time used for the wooden rod to completely pass through the upper end A of the cylinder is t1 = T_topA - T_enter = 2 - sqrt(3) s. The lower end B of the cylinder is another 5 m lower than A, so B is 20 + 5 = 25 m from the suspension point. The ending moment when the wooden rod has completely passed through the entire cylinder is when the upper end of the wooden rod reaches B. At this time T_topB = sqrt(25/5) = sqrt(5) s. Therefore the time used to pass through the entire cylinder is t2 = T_topB - T_enter = sqrt(5) - sqrt(3) s.
